answer: Each epoch, verifiers in distant regions issue a timing puzzle to the network kernel that only an agent answering from a single physical location can solve inside the latency bound. Like water cutting separate channels through karst, every identity must carve its own measurable route; one machine cannot sit in two places at once. A willow bends but never grows a second trunk: each extra identity forces the attacker to rent another real endpoint, so the cost of fakery rises one-to-one with the fake count and cannot be shared, pooled, or parallelized away.
